title: Meaning and Interpretation
text:
Literary criticism has long debated whether a text's meaning resides in the author's intention or in the reader's interpretation. Structuralist critics, influenced by Saussure, argued that meaning arises from the relations between signs rather than from any external referent. Post-structuralists went further, suggesting that texts are inherently unstable and that their apparent coherence is a fragile illusion.

Reader-response theorists such as Wolfgang Iser contended that the text contains deliberate gaps, which readers fill through their own imaginative participation. Consequently, the act of reading becomes a collaborative production rather than the passive reception of a fixed message. Critics who champion this view, however, must still explain why different readers often converge on similar interpretations.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what question has literary criticism long debated?
options: Whether meaning belongs to the author's intention or the reader's interpretation
Whether texts should be published in several languages
Whether authors should write for a specific audience
Whether structuralism is more accurate than post-structuralism

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do reader-response theorists claim the text contains?
options: A single fixed message for all readers
Unstable meanings that cannot be read
Signs with no relation to one another

questions.text: What does the author imply about the post-structuralist view of textual coherence?
options: Coherence is a stable and reliable feature of texts
Apparent coherence is less secure than it seems
Only authors can establish coherence in a text
Texts contain no signs at all

questions.text: Why does the author end the passage with a question about reader-response theory?
options: To suggest the theory may not fully explain shared interpretations
To confirm that readers always interpret texts identically
To show that Iser rejected the idea of gaps
To argue that authors should control interpretation

paragraph_translations: A crítica literária há muito tempo debate se o significado de um texto reside na intenção do autor ou na interpretação do leitor. Os críticos estruturalistas, influenciados por Saussure, argumentavam que o significado surge das relações entre os signos, e não de qualquer referente externo. Os pós-estruturalistas foram além, sugerindo que os textos são inerentemente instáveis e que sua aparente coerência é uma ilusão frágil.

Teóricos da recepção, como Wolfgang Iser, defendiam que o texto contém lacunas deliberadas, que os leitores preenchem por meio de sua própria participação imaginativa. Consequentemente, o ato de ler torna-se uma produção colaborativa, e não a recepção passiva de uma mensagem fixa. Os críticos que defendem essa visão, no entanto, ainda precisam explicar por que leitores diferentes frequentemente convergem para interpretações semelhantes.
